questions.original: If you could keep one thing from every age you have been so far, what would it be?
questions.paraphrased: Which age gave you your best memory, your best laugh, and your most important lesson?

vocab.definition: to continue to have or hold something
something you remember from the past

possibleAnswers: I would keep the energy of my twenties and the calm of my thirties.
The best laugh came from a silly moment with friends in school.
My most important lesson was learning that patience fixes most problems.

questions.original: What is something you understand now that you did not understand when you were younger?
questions.paraphrased: How has your way of seeing the world changed as you have grown?

vocab.definition: to know what something means or how it works
to become bigger, older, or more developed

possibleAnswers: I now understand that most people are doing their best.
I used to think being busy meant being important. Now I know rest matters too.
I understand my parents much better than I did as a teenager.

questions.original: What advice would you give to your younger self on their first day of secondary school?
questions.paraphrased: What would have helped you most back then, and what would you tell them now?

vocab.definition: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do
sure of yourself and your abilities

possibleAnswers: I would tell them to be confident and join a club early.
I would say that the people who matter will like you for who you are.
I would remind them that awkward phases do not last forever.

questions.original: What is the best thing about being the age you are right now?
questions.paraphrased: What can you do, know, or enjoy today that you could not before?

vocab.definition: the power to do what you want without limits
the act of deciding between two or more options

possibleAnswers: I love the freedom to make my own choices.
I understand myself better, so I make better decisions.
I can enjoy simple things like a quiet evening without feeling bored.

questions.original: Who is the most interesting older person you know, and what have they taught you?
questions.paraphrased: What life experience or story of theirs stays with you?

vocab.definition: knowledge or skill from doing something over time
having good judgement based on experience

possibleAnswers: My grandfather taught me that hard work is quieter than people think.
A former neighbour showed me how to stay curious at any age.
My old teacher taught me that asking questions is never embarrassing.

questions.original: If you could sit down with your eighty-year-old self for one conversation, what would you ask?
questions.paraphrased: What do you hope they will tell you about the years in between?

vocab.definition: a talk between two or more people
a feeling of sadness about something you did or did not do

possibleAnswers: I would ask if the risks I took were worth it.
I would ask which friendships they kept and which they let go.
I would ask what they wish they had started sooner.

questions.original: What is a skill or hobby you want to learn that people of any age can start?
questions.paraphrased: Why does it appeal to you, and what would your first step be?

vocab.definition: an ability to do something well
an activity you enjoy in your free time

possibleAnswers: I want to learn the guitar because music makes people happy.
I would love to learn cooking proper meals from scratch.
I have always wanted to try photography and capture light beautifully.

questions.original: What moment from your life so far would you replay if you could?
questions.paraphrased: What made it special, and who was there with you?

vocab.definition: a very short period of time
better or more important than usual

possibleAnswers: I would replay the day I graduated — the pride on my family's faces.
A summer evening with friends by the lake would be my choice.
The moment my team won the final match would never get old.

questions.original: What do you think makes a person 'young at heart'?
questions.paraphrased: Do you know someone who is young at heart? What do they do differently?

vocab.definition: eager to know or learn new things
enjoying fun and games; not always serious

possibleAnswers: Being curious and playful keeps people young at heart.
My aunt is young at heart because she tries new things all the time.
I think it is about laughing often and not taking yourself too seriously.

questions.original: What is something you are looking forward to in the next ten years?
questions.paraphrased: What small steps could you take this year to move towards it?

vocab.definition: to feel happy and excited about something in the future
to succeed in doing or reaching something

possibleAnswers: I look forward to building my own home.
I want to achieve fluency in a second language.
I am excited to see my children grow into interesting adults.

questions.original: What is a tradition in your family that connects the generations?
questions.paraphrased: How did it start, and what do the youngest members think of it?

vocab.definition: a custom or belief passed from parents to children
all the people born around the same time

possibleAnswers: Every Sunday we cook the same soup my grandmother made.
We play cards after Christmas dinner — even the kids join now.
We take a photo in the same spot every year.

questions.original: What do you think people get wrong about getting older?
questions.paraphrased: What positive side of ageing do people rarely mention?

vocab.definition: to believe something is true without proof
something that helps you or puts you in a better position

possibleAnswers: People assume getting older means slowing down, but many stay active.
The advantage of ageing is knowing what truly matters.
People forget that older people can be the most fun to talk to.

questions.original: What would you tell someone who is nervous about turning thirty?
questions.paraphrased: What do you actually know about that age from people who have lived it?

vocab.definition: worried or slightly afraid about something
unhappy because you keep thinking about a problem

possibleAnswers: I would say thirty is when you finally start trusting yourself.
Nothing magical changes at midnight — the cake is the best part.
I would tell them their best years are ahead, not behind.

questions.original: What is a question you would love to ask your grandparents, if they were here?
questions.paraphrased: What do you imagine their answer would be?

vocab.definition: to form a picture or idea of something in your mind
the story of past events

possibleAnswers: I would ask how they met — I imagine it was in a dance hall.
I would ask what their biggest fear was during the war years.
I would ask what made them happiest about raising my parent.

questions.original: What is something you have done recently that your younger self would be proud of?
questions.paraphrased: What does that say about how you have grown?

vocab.definition: feeling pleased about something you or others did
to make or become better

possibleAnswers: I finally started the business I always dreamed about.
I ran a half marathon — younger me would not believe it.
I stood up for a colleague at work, which I could not do before.

questions.original: What age do you think people are at their most creative, and why?
questions.paraphrased: What examples from your own life or others support your idea?

vocab.definition: good at making new things or new ideas
to help show that something is true

possibleAnswers: Children are creative because they are not afraid to be wrong.
I think people in their forties are creative because they know their craft.
Creativity can bloom at any age — it is about staying curious.

questions.original: What is one feature of your appearance that you have learned to appreciate?
questions.paraphrased: What made you start to see it differently?

vocab.definition: to recognise the good qualities of something
a noticeable part of your face or body

possibleAnswers: I have learned to appreciate my freckles — they make me unique.
My height used to bother me, now I see it as an advantage.
I appreciate my smile because people always say it is warm.

questions.original: If you could choose any style, with no rules and no judgement, what would you wear?
questions.paraphrased: What stops people from dressing that way in real life?

vocab.definition: a particular way of dressing or doing things
an opinion about someone, often negative

possibleAnswers: I would wear bright colours every day — life is too short for grey.
I would dress like a 1920s film star for the whole week.
I would mix formal jackets with hiking boots and not apologise.

questions.original: What does your style say about you?
questions.paraphrased: How has your style changed as you have become more yourself?

vocab.definition: a particular way of dressing or doing things
feeling relaxed and at ease

possibleAnswers: My style says I value comfort first and fun second.
I dress more boldly now because I feel more comfortable in my skin.
My style is practical — it shows I have places to go.

questions.original: Who has influenced the way you look, and how?
questions.paraphrased: Did you copy anyone as a teenager? What would you tell that younger you now?

vocab.definition: to affect how someone thinks or behaves
to do or make the same as someone else

possibleAnswers: My older sister influenced me — I copied her haircuts for years.
A film character shaped my style when I was fifteen.
My grandmother taught me that posture changes everything.

questions.original: What is the best compliment you have ever received about your appearance?
questions.paraphrased: Why did that one stick with you more than the others?

vocab.definition: a nice thing you say about someone
sure of yourself and your abilities

possibleAnswers: Someone said my eyes change colour in the light — I loved that.
A friend said I always look like I know where I am going.
My mum told me I look happiest when I am not trying too hard.

questions.original: What does 'looking after yourself' mean to you?
questions.paraphrased: Which part — sleep, food, exercise, rest — makes the biggest difference for you?

vocab.definition: a regular way of doing things
the strength and enthusiasm to do things

possibleAnswers: For me it is a simple routine: enough sleep and a walk outside.
Eating well gives me energy, so that is my priority.
Looking after yourself means listening to what your body needs.

questions.original: If your reflection could talk, what would you want it to say to you?
questions.paraphrased: What do you think it would say now, honestly?

vocab.definition: the image you see in a mirror or water
in a truthful way

possibleAnswers: I would want it to say I look kind, because that matters most.
I hope it would say I am trying my best, and that is enough.
I would want it to notice my laugh lines — proof of good times.

questions.original: How do you think beauty standards have changed since your parents were young?
questions.paraphrased: Which change do you think is for the better?

vocab.definition: a level of quality that people expect
including many different types of people

possibleAnswers: Beauty standards are more diverse now, which is wonderful.
Social media made them narrower in some ways, but broader in others.
I think people care less about perfection now and more about personality.

questions.original: What is one thing about your appearance that makes you feel like you?
questions.paraphrased: If you had to lose it, what would you miss most?

vocab.definition: who you are and what makes you different from others
being the only one of its kind

possibleAnswers: My curly hair is part of my identity — I would miss it terribly.
My glasses make me feel like me; I feel strange without them.
My hands — I am a musician, and they are part of my story.

questions.original: What do you notice first about a person's appearance, and why?
questions.paraphrased: Does that change once you get to know them?

vocab.definition: to see or become aware of something
the look on someone's face that shows their feelings

possibleAnswers: I notice their smile — it changes the whole face.
I notice eyes because they show expression and honesty.
Once I know someone, I stop noticing their appearance at all.

questions.original: What would the world lose if everyone looked the same?
questions.paraphrased: What do our differences give us?

vocab.definition: a way in which people or things are not the same
who you are and what makes you different from others

possibleAnswers: We would lose the stories written on our faces.
Difference is what makes families, cultures and art interesting.
Our identities would become invisible — that would be a great loss.

questions.original: What game did you play as a child that you could play for hours without getting bored?
questions.paraphrased: Who did you play it with, and what were the rules?

vocab.definition: the ability to create pictures or ideas in your mind
to create something new for the first time

possibleAnswers: We invented a street game with a ball and a wall — endless fun.
I played imaginary worlds with my cousins every summer.
Hide and seek in the garden was unbeatable.

questions.original: What is a smell, sound, or taste that instantly takes you back to your childhood?
questions.paraphrased: Where does it take you, and who is with you in that memory?

vocab.definition: something you remember from the past
happening immediately, without delay

possibleAnswers: The smell of rain on hot pavement takes me straight to summer holidays.
Fresh bread reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen.
A certain song instantly brings back road trips with my family.

questions.original: What was your favourite place to hide, and what made it perfect?
questions.paraphrased: What did you do while you were hidden in there?

vocab.definition: known only by you or a few people
quiet and calm

possibleAnswers: Behind the garden shed — it was my secret reading spot.
Under my bed with a torch and a comic book.
Up in the tree house, which felt a million miles from everything.

questions.original: What is the bravest thing you remember doing as a child?
questions.paraphrased: How did you feel before, during, and after?

vocab.definition: not afraid to do difficult or scary things
worried or slightly afraid about something

possibleAnswers: I gave a speech in front of the whole school — terrifying and amazing.
I defended a friend who was being teased. I was shaking, but I did it.
I went to a new school knowing nobody. That took real courage.

questions.original: Which book or film from your childhood shaped how you see the world?
questions.paraphrased: What idea from it still stays with you today?

vocab.definition: to affect how someone thinks or behaves
to form a picture or idea of something in your mind

possibleAnswers: The Little Prince taught me that what is essential is invisible.
A nature documentary made me love animals for life.
A fantasy series taught me that ordinary people can be heroes.

questions.original: What did you want to be when you grew up, and what does that say about you?
questions.paraphrased: Did that dream change? What replaced it?

vocab.definition: a strong wish to achieve something
a hope or wish for the future

possibleAnswers: I wanted to be an astronaut — I still love the night sky.
I wanted to be a teacher, and I ended up training people at work.
I dreamed of being a footballer; now I just coach my kids' team.

questions.original: What is a funny habit you had as a child that you still have today?
questions.paraphrased: What would your childhood self think of you now?

vocab.definition: something you do regularly without thinking
to know someone or something because you have seen them before

possibleAnswers: I still talk to myself when I am concentrating. I always have.
I still eat the crusts of the bread first. Some things never change.
I still line up my shoes before bed — my childhood self would recognise me.

questions.original: What did your childhood bedroom say about you?
questions.paraphrased: What would you fill it with now, if you had the same freedom?

vocab.definition: to make something look more attractive by adding things
to bring together things you are interested in

possibleAnswers: Mine was covered in posters of bands and footballers.
I collected stones and shells on every windowsill.
My bedroom was my kingdom — I decorated every corner.

questions.original: What was your most treasured possession as a child, and where is it now?
questions.paraphrased: What made it so precious to you?

vocab.definition: to value something very much
very important and loved

possibleAnswers: A soft toy bear — he still sits on my shelf at home.
My first football, signed by the whole team.
A notebook of drawings that I still keep in a drawer.

questions.original: What did your childhood teach you about friendship that is still true?
questions.paraphrased: Which childhood friend are you still in touch with, if any?

vocab.definition: always supporting your friends
to believe that someone is honest and reliable

possibleAnswers: Childhood taught me that loyalty matters more than popularity.
My best friend from age six is still my best friend today.
I learned that real friends forgive quickly and laugh loudly.

questions.original: If you could give your childhood self one superpower, what would it be?
questions.paraphrased: What problem in your childhood life would that superpower solve?

vocab.definition: an imaginary special ability, like flying or invisibility
to keep someone safe from harm

possibleAnswers: Invisibility — perfect for hiding from chores and playing pranks.
The power to fly, so I could visit my cousins anytime.
The power to make anyone laugh, to cheer up sad days.

questions.original: What is a skill from your childhood that still helps you today?
questions.paraphrased: How did you learn it back then, and how do you use it now?

vocab.definition: an ability to do something well
useful and related to real situations

possibleAnswers: Riding a bike taught me balance — in life and on two wheels.
Building with LEGO gave me patience for solving problems.
Climbing trees made me fearless about heights, which helps at work.

questions.original: What is the kindest thing a grown-up did for you when you were small?
questions.paraphrased: How has that kindness stayed with you?

vocab.definition: caring and nice to other people
to keep something in your mind

possibleAnswers: A teacher stayed after class to help me with maths until I got it.
My uncle always made time to listen — really listen.
A stranger returned my lost teddy bear. I still remember that kindness.

questions.original: What did you love about the place you grew up in?
questions.paraphrased: What would you show a visitor there today?

vocab.definition: the area around where you live
to feel comfortable and accepted somewhere

possibleAnswers: I loved the neighbourhood — everyone knew everyone.
The forest behind our house was my whole world.
I would show them the bakery, the school, and the corner where we played.

questions.original: If you could spend one perfect day anywhere in the world, where would you go and what would you do?
questions.paraphrased: Who would you take with you, and what would make that day perfect?

vocab.definition: so good it could not be better
the place you are travelling to

possibleAnswers: A quiet beach with good books and no alarms.
Tokyo — exploring food stalls from morning to night.
My hometown, revisiting every place I loved growing up.

questions.original: Would you rather have the power to speak every language or the power to play every instrument?
questions.paraphrased: Which one would change your life more, and how?

vocab.definition: the ability to do something
to share information or feelings with others

possibleAnswers: Languages — I could communicate with anyone on Earth.
Instruments — music connects people without words.
Languages, because my work would improve overnight.

questions.original: If you had to live in one season for the rest of your life, which would you choose?
questions.paraphrased: What would you miss most about the other three?

vocab.definition: one of the four parts of the year
warm, comfortable and relaxing

possibleAnswers: Autumn — cozy sweaters, golden light and calm energy.
Summer — long evenings and the sea.
Spring — everything coming back to life.

questions.original: Would you rather be a famous artist nobody knows personally, or unknown but deeply loved by your community?
questions.paraphrased: What does your answer say about what you value?

vocab.definition: known by many people
the people who live or work together in one place

possibleAnswers: Loved by my community — that is a real life.
Fame sounds lonely; I would rather matter to a few people deeply.
Being known worldwide means my work reaches more people.

questions.original: If you could instantly master one skill without practising, what would you choose?
questions.paraphrased: What would you do with that skill in the first week?

vocab.definition: to learn something so well you are an expert
an ability to do something well

possibleAnswers: Cooking — I would throw a dinner party for everyone I love.
Playing piano — I would play for my grandmother.
Surfing — I would move to the coast immediately.

questions.original: Would you rather always be early or always be exactly on time?
questions.paraphrased: How does being early or late change how people see you?

vocab.definition: arriving at the right time, not late
someone you can trust to do what they promise

possibleAnswers: Always early — I hate rushing and love a quiet coffee first.
Exactly on time is polite and doesn't waste anyone's day.
Early people seem reliable, so I would choose that.

questions.original: If you could choose your perfect job's schedule, what would a typical week look like?
questions.paraphrased: What would you do with the free time you created?

vocab.definition: a plan of when things will happen
able to change easily to fit new situations

possibleAnswers: Three long workdays, then four days for my own projects.
Morning work and afternoon adventures.
A flexible schedule with time to exercise and see friends.

questions.original: Would you rather explore space or explore the deep ocean?
questions.paraphrased: What would you hope to find there?

vocab.definition: to travel somewhere to learn about it
to find something for the first time

possibleAnswers: The ocean — we know so little about what is down there.
Space — the view of Earth would change me forever.
The ocean, because it is right here and full of mystery.

questions.original: Would you rather read minds or see the future?
questions.paraphrased: Which one would cause more problems in real life?

vocab.definition: to say what will happen in the future
personal and not meant for others to know

possibleAnswers: Reading minds would ruin trust — people need privacy.
Seeing the future would remove all the fun of surprises.
Reading minds, so I could understand people better.

questions.original: If you could relive one year of your life with everything you know now, which year would you pick?
questions.paraphrased: What would you do differently the second time?

vocab.definition: to experience something again in your mind
a chance to do something good

possibleAnswers: My final year of school — I would worry less and join more clubs.
The year I moved abroad — I would say yes to more invitations.
I would pick a happy year and just enjoy it twice.

questions.original: Would you rather be the person who starts great ideas or the person who finishes them perfectly?
questions.paraphrased: Which role are you naturally better at?

vocab.definition: a thought or plan about what to do
to finish something fully

possibleAnswers: I am a starter — my head is full of ideas.
Finishing is where the magic happens, so I would choose that.
A good team needs both, but personally I love the finishing.

questions.original: If you had to give up one modern convenience forever, which could you live without?
questions.paraphrased: Which one could you never give up, and why?

vocab.definition: something that makes life easier
completely necessary

possibleAnswers: I could give up the car — walking is good for me.
Never my phone — it connects me to everyone I love.
I could live without delivery apps, but never without hot water.

questions.original: Would you rather have a map that shows you the best route in life or a compass that shows the right direction?
questions.paraphrased: What is the difference between knowing the steps and knowing the way?

vocab.definition: the way something is going or pointing
the reason something is done or exists

possibleAnswers: A compass — the right direction matters more than the exact steps.
A map — I like knowing what comes next.
A compass, because life changes and the route must change with it.

questions.original: If you could choose the soundtrack of your life, what kind of music would play at your best moments?
questions.paraphrased: What song would play right now?

vocab.definition: the music that plays during a film or event
a very short period of time

possibleAnswers: Upbeat, energetic music for adventures.
Soft acoustic songs for quiet, happy moments.
A song that makes me feel unstoppable would be on repeat.

questions.original: What is the strangest dream you have ever had that you still remember?
questions.paraphrased: What do you think your brain was trying to work through?

vocab.definition: unusual or surprising
to keep something in your mind

possibleAnswers: I dreamed I was flying over my town on a giant fish.
I once dreamed in a language I do not speak. Very strange.
I dreamed I was late to an exam made of spaghetti.

questions.original: If dreams are stories your mind tells at night, what genre is your most common dream?
questions.paraphrased: An adventure, a comedy, a mystery — what does that say about you?

vocab.definition: a style or type of story, film or music
an exciting experience

possibleAnswers: Mine are mostly adventures — I am always running somewhere.
My dreams are comedies — ridiculous situations that make no sense.
Mostly peaceful nature scenes, which I love.

questions.original: Have you ever woken up from a dream feeling a strong emotion? Which one?
questions.paraphrased: How long did that feeling stay with you during the day?

vocab.definition: a strong feeling like joy, fear or love
the happy feeling when something bad ends

possibleAnswers: I woke up crying from a sad dream once. It stayed all morning.
A dream about winning something left me excited all day.
Relief — I dreamed I lost my passport, then woke up and it was fine.

questions.original: What do you think dreams are for?
questions.paraphrased: Are they practice, problem-solving, or just mental noise?

vocab.definition: an idea that tries to explain something
to deal with information or feelings

possibleAnswers: I think dreams help us process the day's feelings.
Maybe they are the brain tidying up and filing memories.
I believe some dreams are just fun — nothing more.

questions.original: If you could control your dreams tonight, what dream would you design?
questions.paraphrased: What would the setting, the people, and the ending be?

vocab.definition: to plan how something will look or work
the final part of a story

possibleAnswers: Flying over beautiful mountains with my favourite music.
A dream dinner with everyone I miss.
An adventure where I am brave and everything goes right.

questions.original: Do you usually remember your dreams, or do they disappear the moment you wake up?
questions.paraphrased: What helps you remember them — writing them down, telling someone?

vocab.definition: to stop being seen or to vanish
a small piece of information

possibleAnswers: They disappear fast, so I tell my partner before I forget.
I remember vivid ones and forget the rest.
I keep a notebook by the bed for the good ones.

questions.original: Have you ever had the same dream more than once? What was it?
questions.paraphrased: Why do you think it keeps coming back?

vocab.definition: to happen again
well known to you

possibleAnswers: I keep dreaming about being back at school and forgetting my locker.
A recurring dream about a house with rooms I have never seen.
Yes — falling dreams, which everyone seems to have.

questions.original: What is the most beautiful dream you have ever had?
questions.paraphrased: Describe the colours, the feeling, and the people in it.

vocab.definition: very pleasing to look at or experience
quiet and calm

possibleAnswers: I dreamed I was walking through a golden field at sunset.
A dream where I met a relative who had passed — it felt so real.
Floating in warm, clear water under a huge sky.

questions.original: If dreams could send you a message, what message would you most like to receive tonight?
questions.paraphrased: What do you need to hear right now?

vocab.definition: information sent from one person to another
to give someone hope or confidence

possibleAnswers: That everything will work out, and I am on the right path.
A message from someone I miss, saying they are proud of me.
Just a reminder to slow down and enjoy today.

questions.original: Some people say dreams solve problems. Has a dream ever helped you with something in real life?
questions.paraphrased: What was the problem, and what did the dream show you?

vocab.definition: to find the answer to a problem
a way of solving a problem

possibleAnswers: I dreamed about a work problem and woke up with the answer.
A dream reminded me where I left my keys — embarrassing but true!
I dreamed a conversation with a friend and it fixed our argument.

questions.original: What would it be like if your dreams were made into a film? What would the title be?
questions.paraphrased: Who would star in it, and would it be a hit or a flop?

vocab.definition: the name of a film, book or song
the ability to create pictures or ideas in your mind

possibleAnswers: Title: 'Never Late Again' — a thriller about missing buses.
It would be a beautiful nature film with no plot at all.
A comedy starring me, losing everything and finding it again.

questions.original: Do you think animals dream? What do you imagine your pet dreams about?
questions.paraphrased: What do their sleeping movements tell you?

vocab.definition: to form a picture or idea of something in your mind
the way a person or animal acts

possibleAnswers: My dog definitely dreams about chasing things — his legs run!
Cats probably dream about food and sunny windows.
I imagine my pet dreams about me coming home.

questions.original: What is your favourite smell, and what memory is attached to it?
questions.paraphrased: Where would you bottle that smell if you could?

vocab.definition: something you remember from the past
to connect something to something else

possibleAnswers: Fresh coffee — it means a slow morning with a book.
Rain on warm earth — it reminds me of childhood summers.
My grandmother's perfume, which I still recognise everywhere.

questions.original: What is your favourite sound in the world?
questions.paraphrased: What sound instantly calms you or makes you smile?

vocab.definition: something you hear
relaxed and not worried

possibleAnswers: Rain on the window — instant calm.
My children laughing together.
The sea — it makes any problem feel smaller.

questions.original: What is your favourite time of day, and what do you usually do then?
questions.paraphrased: What makes that hour special for you?

vocab.definition: a regular way of doing things
quiet and calm

possibleAnswers: Early morning, before the world wakes up — coffee and quiet.
Golden hour in the evening, when the light turns soft.
Late night, when I finally get time for myself.

questions.original: What is the best meal you have ever eaten, and where were you?
questions.paraphrased: Who was with you, and what made it unforgettable?

vocab.definition: worth remembering; special
a special event or time

possibleAnswers: A pasta dish in a tiny Italian village — the sauce was magic.
My mother's birthday dinner, with the whole family around the table.
Street food in Bangkok at midnight. Unforgettable.

questions.original: What is your favourite place to think, and why does it work for you?
questions.paraphrased: What do you usually think about when you are there?

vocab.definition: easy to understand; not confused
to rest and become calm

possibleAnswers: A long walk by the river — my head clears instantly.
My balcony with a coffee, watching the street below.
In the shower, where all my best ideas appear!

questions.original: What is your favourite way to spend a completely free Sunday?
questions.paraphrased: What is the perfect balance of doing and resting for you?

vocab.definition: free time when you can relax
to get your energy back

possibleAnswers: Slow breakfast, a long walk, and a film in the evening.
Doing absolutely nothing until noon. Glorious.
Meeting friends for lunch, then reading until dinner.

questions.original: What is your favourite piece of technology, and how has it improved your life?
questions.paraphrased: What would life be like without it for a week?

vocab.definition: to make or become better
completely necessary

possibleAnswers: My phone — it keeps me close to family far away.
My headphones — music makes every day better.
The camera on my phone, because I never miss a moment now.

questions.original: What is your favourite season, and what do you love most about it?
questions.paraphrased: What does that season give you that the others cannot?

vocab.definition: one of the four parts of the year
the feeling or mood of a place

possibleAnswers: Autumn — the colours and the cozy atmosphere.
Summer — long light evenings and warm nights.
Winter — snow, silence, and hot drinks.

questions.original: What is your favourite childhood meal that you would still order today?
questions.paraphrased: Has the way you eat it changed since you were small?

vocab.definition: food that makes you feel good and reminds you of home
the instructions for making a dish

possibleAnswers: My mum's potato soup — still my number one.
The same pizza place from my childhood. Some things never change.
Grilled cheese, exactly how my dad made it.

questions.original: What is your favourite way to celebrate something good?
questions.paraphrased: What is your personal celebration ritual?

vocab.definition: to do something special for a happy event
a custom or habit that is repeated

possibleAnswers: A dinner with the people who helped me get there.
Buying myself a small gift and taking a day off.
Calling everyone I love to share the news.

questions.original: What is your favourite word in any language, and why do you love it?
questions.paraphrased: What does it sound like, and what does it make you feel?

vocab.definition: the idea that a word or action expresses
to say a word in the correct way

possibleAnswers: I love the German word 'Gemütlichkeit' — coziness with people.
'Serendipity' — finding something wonderful by accident.
The Italian word for tomorrow — 'domani'. It sounds hopeful.

questions.original: What is your favourite view, from a place you have actually been?
questions.paraphrased: What did you feel when you first saw it?

vocab.definition: what you can see from a place
so beautiful it surprises you

possibleAnswers: The Alps from a mountain hut at sunrise. Breathtaking.
The sea from a cliff in Portugal at sunset.
My city's skyline from a hill I climb every year.

questions.original: What is your favourite thing about your home?
questions.paraphrased: If you could change one thing about it, what would it be?

vocab.definition: feeling relaxed and at ease
an area or room

possibleAnswers: The kitchen — everything happens there.
The light in the living room in the afternoon.
My balcony garden — my small piece of nature.

questions.original: What is a favourite thing you own that cost almost nothing?
questions.paraphrased: Why is it worth so much to you?

vocab.definition: how much something is worth to you
connected to happy memories

possibleAnswers: A stone my daughter gave me from the beach.
A ticket stub from the first concert I ever went to.
A postcard my best friend sent from abroad.

questions.original: When was the last time you felt truly happy, and what were you doing?
questions.paraphrased: What made that moment different from an ordinary one?

vocab.definition: really or completely
normal; not special or different

possibleAnswers: Last weekend, laughing with friends over dinner.
Watching the sunrise after a good night's sleep on holiday.
When my child learned something new and looked so proud.

questions.original: What small thing makes you happy every single day?
questions.paraphrased: Do you notice it, or does it happen without you realising?

vocab.definition: a feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction
something you do regularly without thinking

possibleAnswers: The first sip of coffee in the morning.
A message from a friend, even just one word.
My dog's welcome-home dance.

questions.original: What do you think happiness is made of: moments, people, or something else?
questions.paraphrased: Which ingredient matters most to you?

vocab.definition: one of the things that makes something what it is
to be important

possibleAnswers: People — shared joy is double joy.
Moments — a few perfect ones beat a lifetime of average.
Peace of mind — everything else is easier when you have that.

questions.original: What is something you do that always lifts your mood when you are down?
questions.paraphrased: Who taught you that trick, or did you discover it yourself?

vocab.definition: the way you feel at a particular time
to find something for the first time

possibleAnswers: Going for a run — it resets everything.
Calling my sister, who makes everything funny.
Cooking something complicated. It keeps my hands and mind busy.

questions.original: Do you think happiness is something you find or something you build?
questions.paraphrased: What have you built into your life that makes it happier?

vocab.definition: to create something over time
a regular way of doing things

possibleAnswers: You build it — with routines, people and small daily choices.
A bit of both: you build the conditions and then notice it.
I built a routine of movement and connection, and it changed my life.

questions.original: What is the happiest memory you can replay in your mind in under ten seconds?
questions.paraphrased: What colours, sounds, and faces are in it?

vocab.definition: something you remember from the past
to experience something again in your mind

possibleAnswers: Crossing the finish line of my first race, my family cheering.
My wedding day, everyone dancing.
A summer evening as a kid, chasing fireflies.

questions.original: What makes you proud of yourself right now?
questions.paraphrased: What did it take to get there, and who noticed?

vocab.definition: feeling pleased about something you or others did
to succeed in doing or reaching something

possibleAnswers: Sticking with my fitness routine for a whole year.
Learning to say no when I need to.
Building my career step by step, without shortcuts.

questions.original: If happiness had a recipe with three ingredients, what would yours be?
questions.paraphrased: What would you add if you had a fourth?

vocab.definition: the instructions for making something
a situation where things are in the right amounts

possibleAnswers: Health, connection, and purpose.
Good food, good music, and good people.
Sleep, movement, and laughter. Plus one extra: nature.

questions.original: How do you celebrate other people's happiness?
questions.paraphrased: What was the last happy news you celebrated with someone?

vocab.definition: to do something special for a happy event
to help or encourage someone

possibleAnswers: I text them straight away and ask for details.
I buy flowers or bake something.
I listen properly — sometimes that is the best celebration.

questions.original: What is something you look forward to that is coming soon?
questions.paraphrased: How does looking forward to things change how you feel today?

vocab.definition: to feel happy and excited about something in the future
very happy and enthusiastic about something

possibleAnswers: A holiday with my friends in two months.
The new season of my favourite show.
My sister's visit — I am counting the days.

questions.original: What do you think is the difference between being happy and being content?
questions.paraphrased: Which one are you more of right now?

vocab.definition: peacefully satisfied with what you have
a way in which things are not the same

possibleAnswers: Happy is a burst; content is a steady feeling.
I am more content these days — and that feels like a win.
Happiness needs a reason; contentment is a choice.

questions.original: What is a time someone's small kindness made your whole day?
questions.paraphrased: How did you pay that kindness forward?

vocab.definition: the quality of being caring and nice
to recognise the good qualities of something

possibleAnswers: A stranger paid for my coffee once. I smiled all day.
Someone held the door and said something warm. Simple but huge.
A colleague noticed I was tired and took over a task.

questions.original: What would you tell someone who says they are not a happy person?
questions.paraphrased: What evidence from your own life would you share?

vocab.definition: facts that show something is true
to become different

possibleAnswers: Happiness is a skill you can practise, not a personality type.
I would say I used to think that too, and small changes helped me.
Nobody is happy all the time — that is not the goal.

questions.original: What is one small healthy habit that has made a real difference in your life?
questions.paraphrased: How did you start it, and how did you make it stick?

vocab.definition: something you do regularly without thinking
a good effect or advantage

possibleAnswers: Walking thirty minutes a day — my energy changed completely.
Drinking water first thing in the morning.
Going to bed at the same time — the biggest difference of all.

questions.original: What does a healthy day look like for you, from morning to night?
questions.paraphrased: Which part of that day is hardest to keep up?

vocab.definition: a regular way of doing things
the strength and enthusiasm to do things

possibleAnswers: A walk in the morning, real food at lunch, and an early night.
Movement, sunlight, and at least one conversation that matters.
Honestly? A healthy day starts with a good sleep the night before.

questions.original: What is your favourite way to move your body that does not feel like exercise?
questions.paraphrased: When did you last do it, and how did you feel after?

vocab.definition: moving around and doing things
to get pleasure from something

possibleAnswers: Dancing in the kitchen while cooking.
Cycling to meet friends instead of driving.
Playing football with my kids — it never feels like training.

questions.original: What do you do when you feel your energy dropping in the middle of the day?
questions.paraphrased: What actually works, and what makes it worse?

vocab.definition: the strength and enthusiasm to do things
to get back to normal after being tired or ill

possibleAnswers: A short walk outside — better than any coffee.
Ten minutes with my eyes closed, no phone.
A snack that is real food, not sugar.

questions.original: What is something you have done recently to take care of your mental health?
questions.paraphrased: What made you decide to try it?

vocab.definition: related to the mind
to make something smaller or less

possibleAnswers: I started saying no to things that drain me.
I take a proper lunch break away from my desk now.
I talk to a friend every week — not about problems, just life.

questions.original: What is your relationship with sleep, honestly?
questions.paraphrased: What would you change about it if you could?

vocab.definition: how good or bad something is
to relax and recover your energy

possibleAnswers: I protect my sleep like it is a meeting.
I sleep well but too little. That is my next project.
My sleep quality improved when I stopped looking at my phone in bed.

questions.original: What food makes you feel your best, and what makes you feel your worst?
questions.paraphrased: How quickly do you notice the difference in your body?

vocab.definition: to see or become aware of something
to change or influence something

possibleAnswers: A big salad with everything in it — I feel light and clear.
Greasy fast food tastes great and then I pay for it all afternoon.
I notice sugar affects my mood within an hour.

questions.original: What is a healthy habit you admire in someone else?
questions.paraphrased: Could you see yourself adopting it? What would the first step be?

vocab.definition: to respect and think highly of someone
to start doing something new

possibleAnswers: My colleague runs before work every day. I admire that discipline.
My aunt swims in the lake all year round. Brave and healthy.
A friend always walks after dinner. Simple and clever.

questions.original: How do you know when your body needs a break?
questions.paraphrased: What signals do you notice, and do you listen to them?

vocab.definition: a sign that something is happening
to pay attention to something

possibleAnswers: I get headaches and short-tempered. That is my warning light.
When everything feels like effort, I know I need rest.
I am learning to notice it earlier now — before the crash.

questions.original: What is the difference between being tired and being exhausted?
questions.paraphrased: How do you recover from each one differently?

vocab.definition: needing rest or sleep
extremely tired, with no energy left

possibleAnswers: Tired is fixed by a good night. Exhausted needs a whole weekend.
Tired means one more coffee helps; exhausted means only rest helps.
Exhausted is when even your favourite things feel heavy.

questions.original: What is a health goal you are proud of reaching, however small?
questions.paraphrased: What did you learn about yourself in the process?

vocab.definition: something you aim to achieve
to succeed in doing or reaching something

possibleAnswers: Walking ten thousand steps for thirty days straight.
Cooking five healthy dinners a week for a month.
Running my first five kilometres without stopping.

questions.original: What do you think is more important: eating well or sleeping well?
questions.paraphrased: If you had to give one up for a month, which would you keep?

vocab.definition: having a big effect or value
to decide between things

possibleAnswers: Sleep — everything else collapses without it.
Eating well — good food protects you for decades.
They feed each other, so I refuse to choose!

questions.original: What does 'being healthy' really mean to you?
questions.paraphrased: Is it about the body, the mind, or something bigger?

vocab.definition: a situation where things are in the right amounts
the meaning of a word or idea

possibleAnswers: It means having energy for the life I want to live.
It is a balance — body, mind, and the people around me.
For me it is feeling strong enough to enjoy everything.

questions.original: What is a small change you could make this week that your future self would thank you for?
questions.paraphrased: What would stop you, and how could you get past that?

vocab.definition: to make or become better
the time that is coming after now

possibleAnswers: Going to bed half an hour earlier.
Preparing lunch the night before.
Booking that doctor's appointment I keep postponing.

questions.original: How do you feel after spending time in nature?
questions.paraphrased: What is the shortest nature break that actually works for you?

vocab.definition: the natural world: trees, animals, rivers, sky
relaxed and not worried

possibleAnswers: Even ten minutes in a park changes my whole afternoon.
I feel lighter and more patient after a forest walk.
The sea air does something nothing else can.

questions.original: What is your favourite way to relax after a long week?
questions.paraphrased: What makes it a proper rest rather than just killing time?

vocab.definition: to rest and become calm
to get your energy back

possibleAnswers: A long bath with music and no phone.
A film that makes me laugh out loud.
A slow walk with someone I do not see enough.

questions.original: What would you tell your younger self about looking after their health?
questions.paraphrased: What do you know now that you wish you had known then?

vocab.definition: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do
to keep someone safe from harm

possibleAnswers: Start moving now — your future body will thank you.
Sleep is not lazy. It is maintenance.
You do not need to be perfect, just consistent.

questions.original: What is the fastest way to change your mood when you notice it slipping?
questions.paraphrased: Does it work every time, or are some days different?

vocab.definition: the way you feel at a particular time
to make or become better

possibleAnswers: Music — a song I love changes everything in seconds.
Getting outside, even for two minutes.
Talking to someone who makes me laugh.

questions.original: What kind of music matches your mood when you are happy, and what when you are sad?
questions.paraphrased: Why do we choose different music for different feelings?

vocab.definition: to be the same or go well together
an emotion like happiness or sadness

possibleAnswers: Happy: upbeat pop. Sad: soft acoustic songs.
I listen to energetic music to lift myself out of a bad mood.
Sometimes sad music helps because it understands me.

questions.original: What is a mood you think everyone should experience at least once?
questions.paraphrased: What causes it, and how do you recognise it?

vocab.definition: to live through something
to know something because you have seen it before

possibleAnswers: Pure excitement — the feeling before something wonderful.
Deep calm — the kind after a long hike.
The joy of finishing something you worked hard on.

questions.original: How do your moods affect the people around you?
questions.paraphrased: How do you protect others from your worst moods?

vocab.definition: to change or influence something
knowing that something exists or is happening

possibleAnswers: I am aware my mood spreads, so I warn people when I am off.
I take space when I need it instead of taking it out on others.
A good mood of mine lifts everyone; a bad one drags them too.

questions.original: What is something that always makes you laugh, no matter your mood?
questions.paraphrased: Who is the funniest person you know, and what do they do?

vocab.definition: to make the sound of happiness
making you laugh

possibleAnswers: Videos of animals doing ridiculous things.
My best friend's impressions — they are terrible and hilarious.
The way my dog reacts to his own reflection.

questions.original: Do you think moods are something you control, or something that happens to you?
questions.paraphrased: What is your evidence from your own life?

vocab.definition: to make something do what you want
the act of deciding between two or more options

possibleAnswers: A bit of both — feelings arrive, but my response is my choice.
I used to think moods happened to me. Now I know I can steer them.
Some days are harder than others, but I always have some control.

questions.original: What is a mood you would love to feel more often?
questions.paraphrased: What usually brings it on, and how could you invite it more?

vocab.definition: to ask something to come or happen
relaxed and not worried

possibleAnswers: That calm, content feeling after a good day.
Excitement — I want more things to look forward to.
Playful joy, like when I was a kid.

questions.original: How do you describe your mood right now in three words?
questions.paraphrased: What is behind those three words?

vocab.definition: to say what something is like
telling the truth

possibleAnswers: Curious, calm, a little tired.
Hopeful, busy, happy.
To be honest: mixed. But mostly okay.

questions.original: What is the weather of your mood today — sunny, cloudy, or stormy?
questions.paraphrased: What forecast would you give for tomorrow?

vocab.definition: a prediction of what will happen
full of light or happiness

possibleAnswers: Partly cloudy — some heavy thoughts, some light ones.
Sunny with occasional showers.
Stormy this morning, but clearing up by afternoon.

questions.original: What do you do when a friend is in a bad mood?
questions.paraphrased: What do you wish people did when YOU are in a bad mood?

vocab.definition: to help or encourage someone
to make someone feel better

possibleAnswers: I listen first and fix nothing. That is what they need.
I make them laugh if they want, or sit quietly if they do not.
I wish people would just ask, 'Do you want to talk or distract?'

questions.original: What is a mood that you find hard to express in words?
questions.paraphrased: How do you try to show it instead — through music, art, silence?

vocab.definition: to show or say what you feel
to say what something is like

possibleAnswers: That bittersweet feeling when something ends beautifully.
I express it through music — a song says it better than I can.
The restless feeling of wanting change but not knowing what.

questions.original: What song would be the soundtrack to your mood right now?
questions.paraphrased: What would the next track be?

vocab.definition: the music that plays during a film or event
one song on an album or playlist

possibleAnswers: Something slow and warm, like a Sunday afternoon.
An upbeat song that pretends everything is fine — and then it is.
A calm acoustic track, with something energetic next.

questions.original: What is something that surprises you about your own moods?
questions.paraphrased: What did you learn about yourself recently in this area?

vocab.definition: to make someone feel unexpected wonder
to get new knowledge or skills

possibleAnswers: I am surprised how much sleep changes my whole mood.
I learned that I need alone time after social events, not before.
It surprises me that small victories lift me more than big ones.

questions.original: If you could give everyone one mood-boosting tip, what would it be?
questions.paraphrased: Where did you learn that tip yourself?

vocab.definition: a small piece of useful advice
to give something to other people

possibleAnswers: Move your body for five minutes — it breaks the spiral.
Text someone you love something kind. Giving lifts moods.
Change your scenery, even just a different room.

questions.original: If your personality were a colour, what colour would it be and why?
questions.paraphrased: What would the colour change to when you are tired or excited?

vocab.definition: to say what something is like
to stand for or symbolise something

possibleAnswers: Green — calm, growing, and good in groups.
Blue — deep, thoughtful, a bit mysterious.
Yellow — bright and friendly, but quieter when tired.

questions.original: What is a quality you have that people often notice about you?
questions.paraphrased: What do people compliment you on that you do not see yourself?

vocab.definition: a characteristic or feature of a person
to see or become aware of something

possibleAnswers: People say I am calm in a crisis. I do not always feel it!
My patience — which I practise, not born with.
People notice that I actually listen.

questions.original: Are you more of an early bird or a night owl, and does that match your personality?
questions.paraphrased: What is your best hour of the day for deep thinking?

vocab.definition: the strength and enthusiasm to do things
getting a lot done

possibleAnswers: Night owl — my brain wakes up when the world sleeps.
Early bird — I do my best thinking before breakfast.
I am a 'depends on the day' bird, honestly.

questions.original: What is something about your personality that has changed as you have grown older?
questions.paraphrased: What made that change happen?

vocab.definition: to become different
to grow or become more advanced

possibleAnswers: I used to be shy; now I genuinely enjoy meeting people.
I have become more patient — parenthood did that.
I care less about being liked and more about being honest.

questions.original: What is a personality trait you admire in other people?
questions.paraphrased: Do you have a little of it yourself? Where does it show?

vocab.definition: a quality that is part of someone's character
to respect and think highly of someone

possibleAnswers: Warmth — people who make everyone feel welcome.
Courage — saying the hard thing kindly.
I admire curiosity, and I try to keep mine alive.

questions.original: If you had to describe yourself in one sentence for someone who has never met you, what would it be?
questions.paraphrased: What would your best friend add to that sentence?

vocab.definition: to say what something is like
a short version of the main points

possibleAnswers: Curious, kind, and always slightly late.
A quiet person with loud opinions about food.
Someone who would rather laugh than argue.

questions.original: What brings out the best in you?
questions.paraphrased: What situations, people, or challenges make you shine?

vocab.definition: something difficult that tests your ability
to make someone want to do something good

possibleAnswers: A deadline and a team that believes in me.
Helping someone else — it brings out my best self.
New places. Travel makes me more curious and brave.

questions.original: What is something about your personality that surprised you recently?
questions.paraphrased: What did you do that made you think, 'Oh, so I am that kind of person'?

vocab.definition: to make someone feel unexpected wonder
to find something for the first time

possibleAnswers: I discovered I am actually good at leading a team.
I surprised myself by enjoying something I was terrified to try.
I learned I need quiet after big events — I thought I was an extrovert.

questions.original: Are you a person who plans everything or someone who goes with the flow?
questions.paraphrased: What is the downside of your style, and what is the upside?

vocab.definition: to decide in advance what you will do
doing things suddenly, without planning

possibleAnswers: I plan everything — spontaneity stresses me out.
I go with the flow — plans feel like cages.
I plan the big things and stay flexible with the small ones.

questions.original: What is a small thing you do that shows your personality without you saying a word?
questions.paraphrased: What would someone learn about you from watching you for a day?

vocab.definition: the way a person acts
to watch and notice something carefully

possibleAnswers: I always tidy the table after others. A watcher would see that.
I hum while I work — apparently all the time.
I give people my full attention when they speak.

questions.original: If your life were a book, what genre would it be?
questions.paraphrased: What would the chapter you are living right now be called?

vocab.definition: a style or type of story, film or music
one part of a book or a period of life

possibleAnswers: A comedy with moments of drama.
A slow-burning adventure story.
A slice-of-life novel — quiet but full of small joys.

questions.original: What is one thing you would never change about your personality?
questions.paraphrased: Why is that part of you so important?

vocab.definition: how much something is worth to you
to keep something safe

possibleAnswers: My sense of humour — it has carried me through everything.
My loyalty to the people I love.
My optimism, even when it annoys people.

questions.original: Who in your life brings out a side of you that no one else sees?
questions.paraphrased: What is that side like?

vocab.definition: feeling relaxed and at ease
to believe that someone is honest and reliable

possibleAnswers: My sister — with her I am sillier than anywhere else.
My oldest friend — I can be completely honest with him.
My children bring out my playful side.

topics.title: Do You Think You Are...? (15 questions)

questions.original: What is something you believe about yourself that you are proud of?
questions.paraphrased: What evidence from your life supports that belief?

vocab.definition: feeling pleased about something you or others did
facts that show something is true

possibleAnswers: I believe I am resilient — I have survived every hard year so far.
I am proud that I keep learning, even when it is hard.
I believe I am a good friend, and people tell me so.

questions.original: What is a label people have given you that you actually like?
questions.paraphrased: What is a label you would like to earn in the future?

vocab.definition: a word used to describe a person or group
to say what something is like

possibleAnswers: Someone once called me 'the reliable one'. I loved that.
'Easy to talk to' — that one means a lot.
I would love to be called 'brave' someday.

questions.original: If your closest friend had to describe you in three words, what would they say?
questions.paraphrased: Do you agree with their three words?

vocab.definition: to say what something is like
to have the same opinion as someone

possibleAnswers: They would say: kind, funny, stubborn. Fair enough.
Warm, loyal, and always hungry. Accurate.
They would say calm and steady — I am learning to see that too.

questions.original: What is something you are better at than you give yourself credit for?
questions.paraphrased: Who noticed it before you did?

vocab.definition: recognition or praise for something you did
a natural ability to do something well

possibleAnswers: Listening — I did not realise how rare it is until people told me.
Explaining things simply. My colleagues say I am great at it.
Staying calm under pressure. I always thought that was normal.

questions.original: What would you attempt if you knew you could not fail?
questions.paraphrased: What is the first small step towards that dream?

vocab.definition: to try to do something
sure of yourself and your abilities

possibleAnswers: I would start my own business tomorrow.
I would write and publish a book.
I would move to another country for a year.

questions.original: What is a compliment you have received that you still think about?
questions.paraphrased: Why did it stay with you?

vocab.definition: a nice thing you say about someone
to keep something in your mind

possibleAnswers: My teacher said I had a gift for explaining things. I never forgot it.
Someone said I make people feel safe. That meant everything.
A stranger told me I have a kind face. I think about it often.

questions.original: What is the difference between the person you are and the person you thought you would become?
questions.paraphrased: Which version do you like better, and why?

vocab.definition: to think something will happen
to make someone feel unexpected wonder

possibleAnswers: I thought I would be richer; I did not expect to be this happy.
I expected to be more serious. I am glad I am not.
I am kinder than I planned to be. That is a good surprise.

questions.original: What is something you do that makes you feel like the best version of yourself?
questions.paraphrased: When did you last do it?

vocab.definition: a form of something that is slightly different
to make or become better

possibleAnswers: Helping someone learn something new.
Finishing a workout — I feel unstoppable after.
Making a room full of people laugh.

questions.original: What do you think people misunderstand about you?
questions.paraphrased: What would you want them to know instead?

vocab.definition: to understand something wrongly
to believe something is true without proof

possibleAnswers: People think I am unapproachable because I am quiet. I am just shy.
They assume I am always confident. I am often nervous.
People think I do not care because I am relaxed. I care a lot.

questions.original: If you could be known for one thing, what would you want it to be?
questions.paraphrased: What would you do today to move towards that?

vocab.definition: recognised by many people
to keep something in your mind

possibleAnswers: Being known as someone who made people feel welcome.
As a great teacher who made English fun.
As the person who always showed up for their friends.

questions.original: What is something about yourself that you are still learning to accept?
questions.paraphrased: What makes it difficult, and what is helping?

vocab.definition: to be okay with something
able to wait calmly without getting angry

possibleAnswers: I am learning to accept that I cannot do everything perfectly.
